problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=x(y+1).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\ge 0?$

activity_context.topic_title: Further Solving of Two-Variable Nonlinear Inequalities

feedback.problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=(x-2)(y+1)^{2}.$  What are the missing entries in the sign table of $f(x,y),$ shown below?

| $y>-1$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ |  |  |
|  | $x<2$ | $x>2$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=2$ and $y=-1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/a66a57932dbc935b5ed6f74b4f0faa0047c4b7ef58ded46be088dad30fa5eee4.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/52efe97fcffa3da05151b3ffef5305e0c3ec0d567d3f62b964a30740c08a3981.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x-2)$ | $(y+1)^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(-2,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(4,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-2,-3)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(4,-3)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/aa100568c18b31507c775e77ed3201a5aed6f708b541e48046617a43fe9a8304.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>-1$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ | $-$ | $+$ |
|  | $x<2$ | $x>2$ |
